## Stand-up comedy

[edit]

. He entered the alternative comedy scene in the early 1980s, firstly under the alias Gillian Pieface and later as The Joan Collins Fan Club. He wore heavy glam make-up and dressed in outrageous clothes, often involving leather/PVC and hinting at bondage "Bondage (BDSM)"). His pet dog, Fanny the Wonderdog, a whippet mongrel, also featured in performances.

Since then Clary has undertaken several tours of his stage act, some of which have been released on home video, including:

 The Mincing Machine Tour (1989)
 My Glittering Passage (1993)
 Natural Born Mincer (2003)
 Lord of the Mince (2009–10)
 Position Vacant: Apply Within (2012–13)

| Website | julianclary.co.uk | [...] ## Film

[edit]

Clary appeared in the film Carry On Columbus (1992), an unsuccessful attempt to revive the Carry On series of films. It was widely panned by critics but was more financially profitable than the two other Columbus films released the same year: 1492: Conquest of Paradise and Christopher Columbus: The Discovery.[citation needed]

Clary returned to film in 2001 in The Baby Juice Express, which starred Lisa Faulkner, Samantha Womack, Ruth Jones and David Seaman, about a prisoner who is desperate to find some way of conceiving with his wife while he is in prison but the sperm ends up getting hijacked. It was released on DVD in 2004.

## Radio

[edit]

Clary appeared on The Big Fun Show "The Big Fun Show (radio show)") in 1988.
